issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell immovable property is deemed a conveyance for stamp-duty purposes when possession has been transferred or agreed to be transferred, even if the purchaser’s possession began before the agreement in a different capacity.
Stamp duty is levied on the instrument rather than on the underlying transaction.
Stamp duty already paid on an agreement deemed to be a conveyance must be credited against duty payable on a later conveyance, with recovery limited to the difference and the applicable penalty.
An impounded instrument cannot be used in evidence until the stamp-duty defect is cured as required by law.
